lines: This plan covers 3 days, starting today.
You cook on Tuesday and Saturday, and that is what was kept.
To stay inside it, expensive proteins give first, then out-of-season produce, then variety — never the portions.

dishes.name: Jam toast and eggs
dishes.title: Toast, blackcurrant jam and scrambled eggs
dishes.method: Toast the bread. Scramble the eggs in butter in a pan and serve them beside the toast with blackcurrant jam on the side for Odalric, with crusts cut off for Wilfrid.
dishes.why: A warm breakfast fits the coach’s rule, and the traybake plan leaves room for the house’s Sunday cake later in the stretch.

dishes.name: Traybake lunch boxes
dishes.title: Chicken traybake, roasted potatoes and green beans
dishes.method: Reheat a portion of the traybake, pile it on the plate with the roasted potatoes and green beans, and finish with lemon. Add the salad fresh.
dishes.why: One loud vegetable is covered by the green beans, and this is the first use of the batch before Thursday’s kitchen disruption.

dishes.name: Traybake dinner bowls
dishes.title: Chicken traybake, roasted potatoes and green beans
dishes.method: Reheat a portion of the traybake, potatoes and green beans in a pan or the oven, then finish with lemon. Keep the plates warm because dinner must have a warm element.
dishes.why: It reuses the Wednesday cook while staying within the coach’s no-salad-dinner rule and keeping the evening simple before the shared kitchen day.

dishes.name: Pasta chicken bowls
dishes.title: Chicken, tomato and spinach pasta
dishes.method: Reheat a portion of the chicken sauce, boil the pasta fresh, toss together with spinach and finish with lemon and cheese. This keeps lunch away from the dust sheet and makes the starch follow the session.
dishes.why: Thursday is awkward in the kitchen, so lunch is built from the Wednesday batch and one fresh pot of pasta without needing the table.

dishes.name: Egg fried rice
dishes.title: Egg fried rice with peppers and spring onions
dishes.method: Fry the cold rice with the eggs, peppers and spring onions in a hot pan, finishing with soy sauce. Make it fresh because cooked rice stays within the same day or the day after.
dishes.why: This gives the house a quick dinner that fits the coach’s warm-element rule while avoiding a rice batch that would overrun the safe window.

dishes.name: Traybake salad plates
dishes.title: Chicken traybake, roasted potatoes and green beans
dishes.method: Reheat the remaining traybake and potatoes, add the last green beans, then serve with lemon and salad. This uses the final box before the three-day limit closes.
dishes.why: Friday lunch finishes the Wednesday batch in time and keeps the plate varied enough to avoid the grey-box feeling the coach dislikes.

dishes.name: Traybake supper
dishes.title: Chicken traybake, roasted potatoes and green beans
dishes.method: Reheat the last portion in the oven or a pan, then finish with lemon. Keep it warm and plain, because the house wants comfort after a week with the kitchen table covered.
dishes.why: Friday dinner clears the final Wednesday preparation safely within the three-day window and uses the same base in a different meal context.

dishes.name: Traybake start
dishes.title: Chicken traybake with roasted potatoes and green beans
dishes.method: Toss the chicken thighs, potatoes, onions, garlic, oil and paprika, then roast on trays. Blanch or roast the green beans separately and finish everything with lemon. Box the food hot into four named portions for each person.
dishes.why: It gives the week a clear cooked anchor and a loud green vegetable, while keeping the kitchen work inside one Wednesday session.

dishes.name: Chicken pasta sauce
dishes.title: Chicken, tomato and spinach pasta sauce
dishes.method: Brown the chicken, soften the onions and garlic, then simmer with tomatoes and oregano until the sauce is rich. Stir in spinach at the end and box it for quick Thursday and Friday lunches.
dishes.why: Thursday needs food that survives the kitchen disruption, and this sauce turns the session into two lunches without another full cook.

preparations.title: Chicken traybake with roasted potatoes and green beans
preparations.method: Toss the chicken thighs, potatoes, onions, garlic, oil and paprika, then roast on trays. Blanch or roast the green beans separately and finish everything with lemon. Box the food hot into four named portions.

preparations.title: Chicken, tomato and spinach pasta sauce
preparations.method: Brown the chicken, soften the onions and garlic, then simmer with tomatoes and oregano until the sauce is rich. Stir in spinach at the end and box it for quick Thursday and Friday lunches.

preparations.title: Egg fried rice base with peppers and spring onions
preparations.method: Cook the rice on the same day, cool it quickly, then fry it with eggs, peppers and spring onions in a hot pan. Season with soy sauce and sesame oil, and box any extra only for Friday if needed.

preparations.title: Roasted and blanched green beans
preparations.method: Blanch the green beans, then toss with a little oil, salt and lemon so they stay bright and loud. Box them for the traybake meals.

preparations.title: Roasted potatoes
preparations.method: Chunk the potatoes, toss with oil, salt and pepper, and roast until crisp. Box alongside the traybake so the starch is ready when training or tiredness makes the evening late.

preparations.title: Scrambled eggs for toast and rice
preparations.method: Scramble the eggs gently in butter with a splash of milk and a little salt. Box four breakfast portions so the house can have a fast warm start on each day.

cooking_sessions.run_through: Start the oven for the traybake and potatoes. While they roast, brown the chicken for the tomato sauce, then simmer it with onions, garlic, tomatoes and spinach. Blanch the green beans, scramble the eggs, and box everything hot into the named containers.
Cook the rice fresh, cool it quickly, then fry it with eggs, peppers and spring onions. Box the portions straight away for the same-day dinner and the next day’s use if any remains.

member_portions.portion_note: Serve 2 eggs, 120 g roasted potatoes, 150 g chicken traybake, 80 g rice, and 120 g vegetables; for breakfast swap the chicken traybake for 2 slices toast with blackcurrant jam.

preparation_shares.note: Take the same vegetables as everyone else.

member_portions.portion_note: Serve 1 egg, 80 g roasted potatoes, 100 g chicken traybake, 60 g rice, and 90 g vegetables; for breakfast serve 1 slice toast with the eggs and leave the crust off.

preparation_shares.note: Take the same vegetables as everyone else.

member_portions.portion_note: Serve 2 eggs, 120 g roasted potatoes, 150 g chicken traybake, 80 g rice, and 120 g vegetables; for breakfast swap the chicken traybake for 2 slices toast with jam, and keep the plate free of fennel and carrot-coloured sides.

preparation_shares.note: Take the same vegetables as everyone else, without fennel.

member_portions.portion_note: Serve 1 egg, 80 g roasted potatoes, 100 g chicken traybake, 60 g rice, and 90 g vegetables; for breakfast serve 1 slice toast with the eggs and add hot sauce if wanted.

preparation_shares.note: Take the same vegetables as everyone else.
